claims.text: Laser surface remelting refines the as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating microstructure.
Laser-induced microstructural refinement enhances dynamic dislocation pinning.
Laser-induced microstructural refinement promotes more uniform dynamic recrystallization during high-temperature sliding.
Enhanced dislocation pinning and more uniform dynamic recrystallization reduce wear loss.
Enhanced dislocation pinning and more uniform dynamic recrystallization constrain microscopic deformation.
The proposed treatment uses laser pulses with an intensity of 2 MW/cm², a duration of 5 ms, and 50% overlap.
The intended sliding regime is 500–700°C, with testing centered around 600°C.
Laser treatment produces smaller grains in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Laser treatment produces enhanced dislocation-pinning features in the coating.
A refined microstructure increases the density and distribution of grain boundaries.
The additional grain boundaries act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Grain-boundary barriers delay plastic flow during sliding.
The refined microstructure causes dynamic recrystallization to become more uniform during sliding.
At approximately 600°C, the laser-treated coating will have a lower wear rate than the as-deposited coating.
At approximately 600°C, the laser-treated coating will exhibit less localized plastic deformation than the as-deposited coating.
Different wear mechanisms may predominate at lower temperatures or under different loading conditions.
Prior work on laser-modified high-entropy alloys supports improved deformation resistance through grain refinement and dislocation pinning.
